answer: An operator copying one text across 67 aliases therefore pays for 67 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Since the harbor hash is stored at intake, the atlas graph groups the endorsements and the garden audit publishes the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 3 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
